# rhaix

> Server-rendered HTML framework. Rust core, [Rhai](https://rhai.rs) for business
> logic, HTMX over the wire. One file = one component: markup plus a small logic
> block on top, like Astro. No Rust knowledge required, no frontend build, no
> `node_modules`. Deployment is copying one binary.

This file is the complete working reference. If you write `.rhx` from it alone,
you should not need anything else. Full spec: `SYNTAX.md` (Ukrainian),
`SYNTAX.en.md` (English). Ready-made recipes: `examples/cookbook/`.

Diagnostics are in Ukrainian and always carry `file:line:column` in `.rhx`
coordinates.

---

## File format

```
pages/todo.rhx
---
// frontmatter: Rhai. Runs on the server. Never reaches the response.
let todos = db.find("todos", #{ done: false }, #{ sort: "id desc" });
page.title = "ToDo";
---
<h1>{{ page.title }}</h1>
<ul>
  <TodoItem @for={t in todos} @key={t.id} todo={t} />
  <li @if={todos.is_empty()}>Nothing here</li>
</ul>
```

- Opening `---` must be the first non-empty line. Frontmatter is optional.
- Everything below is markup. Frontmatter variables are visible in it.
- Encoding UTF-8. Extension `.rhx`.

## Four rules that cover the whole language

1. Tag starting with a **capital** letter → component from `components/`.
2. Attribute starting with `@` → framework directive, never emitted as HTML.
3. `{ ... }` as an attribute value → Rhai expression; `"..."` → string (may
   contain `{{ }}`).
4. Everything else is plain HTML, emitted as written.

## Directories

| Path | Role | Reachable over HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `pages/**/*.rhx` | page / endpoint | yes, by file path |
| `partials/**/*.rhx` | HTMX fragment | yes, `/components/<lowercase-name>` |
| `api/**/*.rhx` | JSON endpoint | yes, at `/api/<path>` |
| `components/**/*.rhx` | component | no |
| `layouts/main.rhx` | full-document wrapper | no |
| `scripts/*.rhai` | shared functions, visible everywhere | no |
| `middleware.rhx` | runs before every request | no |
| `migrations/*.sql` | applied at startup, in filename order | no |
| `public/**` | static files; `.css`/`.js` auto-included in layout | yes, at `/` |

Routes: `pages/index.rhx` → `/`, `pages/todo.rhx` → `/todo`,
`pages/blog/index.rhx` → `/blog`, `pages/todo/[id].rhx` → `/todo/{id}`
(`req.param("id")`), `pages/blog/[...rest].rhx` → catch-all.

---

## Output and escaping

```html
{{ value }}                  escaped for the context it sits in
{{ raw(html) }}              no escaping — the only way out, and it is visible
{{! comment, never rendered }}
{{ "{{" }}                   a literal double brace
<rhaix:raw>…</rhaix:raw>     a whole block emitted verbatim
```

`()` and `false` render as an **empty string** (so `{{ maybe }}` never prints
`()` or `false`); everything else goes through `to_string()`. `{{-` and `-}}`
trim surrounding whitespace.

Escaping is **context-aware**, so there is nothing to remember:

| Context | What happens |
|---|---|
| text | HTML-escaped |
| attribute | attribute-escaped |
| `href` `src` `action` `formaction` | plus URL scheme check; `javascript:` becomes `#` and is logged |
| `on*` (`onclick`, …) | an expression here is a **compile error** — event handlers cannot come from data |
| inside `<script>` | only `{{ json(x) }}` is allowed |
| inside `<style>` | interpolation is forbidden |

## Directives

```html
<li @if={t.done}>done</li>
<li @else-if={t.urgent}>urgent</li>
<li @else>pending</li>

<li @for={t in todos} @key={t.id}>{{ t.title }}</li>
<li @for={(t, i) in todos}>{{ i }}: {{ t.title }}</li>       <!-- also (v, k) over maps -->
<li @for={n in 1..=5}>{{ n }}</li>                          <!-- and over ranges -->
<li @for={t in todos}>{{ iter.number }} of {{ iter.count }}</li>

<div @class={#{ "active": is_on, "done": t.done }}>        merged with class="..."
<div @style={#{ "width": percent(done, total) }}>           percent() already adds "%"
<div @attr={#{ "disabled": locked, "data-id": t.id }}>     false/() drops the attribute
<div @html={post.body}>       inner HTML, unescaped
<div @text={post.title}>      inner text, escaped
<tr @oob={"#row-" + o.id}>                                  out-of-band swap; sets id too
<div @oob={["#list", "beforeend"]}>                         selector + swap mode
```

`@if` and `@for` on the same element: the loop wraps the condition, so the loop
variable is visible to `@if`.

Counters live in `iter` (`iter.number`, `iter.index`, `iter.count`,
`iter.first`, `iter.last`) — `loop` is a Rhai keyword and cannot be used.

Truthiness for `@if`: `()`, `false`, `0`, `0.0`, `""`, empty array, empty map
are false. Everything else is true.

## Components

```html
<!-- components/TodoItem.rhx -->
---
// props is a map of what the caller passed
let todo = props.todo;
---
<li @class={#{ "done": todo.done }}>{{ todo.title }}</li>
```

```html
<TodoItem todo={t} />
<TodoItem {...attrs} />
<Ui.Card>…</Ui.Card>          <!-- components/ui/Card.rhx -->
```

Slots:

```html
<!-- components/Card.rhx -->
<section>
  <header @if={slots.has("header")}><slot name="header" /></header>
  <slot />                               <!-- default slot -->
  <footer><slot name="footer">fallback</slot></footer>
</section>
```

```html
<Card>
  <template slot="header"><h2>Title</h2></template>
  Body goes into the default slot.
</Card>
```

A component does **not** inherit the caller's scope: it sees only `props`,
`slots` and the globals. Unknown tags and dependency cycles are **compile**
errors, reported before the first request.

## Layout and the fragment rule

`layouts/main.rhx` is the only full document. An explicit `hx-get`/`hx-post`
(header `HX-Request`) gets the page's own markup with no layout —
`req.is_htmx` is true. A **boosted** link/form under `<body hx-boost>`
(`HX-Boosted`) and a history restore get the **full page**: htmx swaps them
into the whole `<body>`, so a bare fragment would wipe the layout.
`req.is_boosted` tells you which. Files in `partials/` are never wrapped.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="uk">
<head>
  <title>{{ page.title ?? "app" }}</title>
  <rhaix:head />        <!-- css, hoisted <style>, htmx + rhaix.js + ui.js, public/*.js (defer) -->
</head>
<body hx-boost="true">
  <main id="main"><slot /></main>
  <rhaix:scripts />     <!-- hoisted component <script> only -->
</body>
</html>
```

Scripts live in `<head>` because htmx only swaps `<body>`: a script at the end
of `<body>` would re-run on every boosted navigation.

`page` is a shared map: set `page.title` in the page, read it in the layout.
`page.layout = "admin"` picks `layouts/admin.rhx`; `page.layout = false` renders
the page with no layout at all.

**The layout does not run on htmx navigation at all** — nothing in it (a nav
menu, a header counter) re-renders itself. Two consequences:

- `<title>` updates automatically: if `page.title` is set, the fragment
  response carries a `<title>` tag and htmx applies it, using the raw
  `page.title` value (not whatever the layout composes around it).
- Anything else persistent (an active nav link, a counter) needs `@oob`
  yourself: wrap a component in an element (`@oob` does not work directly on a
  component tag) and guard it with `@if={req.is_htmx}` so it does not
  duplicate on a full load —

```html
<div @if={req.is_htmx} @oob={"#nav"}><Nav /></div>
```

  See `components/Nav.rhx` in `examples/demo` / `examples/cookbook`.

---

## Globals available in every file

| Name | What |
|---|---|
| `req` | `req.method`, `req.path`, `req.url` (path + query), `req.ip`, `req.is_htmx`, `req.param/query/form/header/cookie`, typed `query_int/query_float/query_bool` and `form_int/form_float/form_bool`, `req.all_query()`, `req.all_form()`, `req.body` |
| `res` | `res.status(422)`, `res.header(k,v)`, `res.cookie(k,v)`, `res.redirect("/login")`, `res.download(name, content[, type])` |
| `hx` | `hx.toast(msg, "success")`, `hx.trigger(name[, detail])`, `hx.redirect`, `hx.refresh`, `hx.push_url`, `hx.retarget`, `hx.reswap`, `hx.location` |
| `db` | see below |
| `session` | `session.set/get/has/remove/clear/all`, `session.user` |
| `csrf` | `csrf.token` |
| `http` | `http.get/post/put/patch/delete` |
| `state` | process-wide key/value: `state.get/set/has/remove`; rate limit: `state.allow(key, max, seconds)`, `state.retry_after(key)`, `state.reset(key)` |
| `page` | shared map for the page and its layout |
| `live` | `live.send(topic[, detail])` — tell open pages that data changed |
| `log` | `log.info/warn/error` |
| `props` `slots` | inside components |
| `iter` | inside `@for` |

Missing values are `()`, so `req.query("x") ?? "default"` is the idiom.

Only `res.redirect`, `hx.redirect` and `hx.refresh` stop rendering.
`res.status(422)` does **not**: re-rendering a form with errors is the normal
case.

## Database

```rhai
// Portable CRUD — works on every driver
db.find("orders", #{ status: "paid" }, #{ sort: "id desc", limit: 20, skip: 40 })
db.get("orders", id)                       // by primary key, () if absent
db.count("orders", #{ status: "new" })
db.insert("orders", #{ customer: name })   // returns the new id
db.update("orders", id, #{ status: "paid" })
db.delete("orders", id)

// Native SQL when you need it — always parameterised
db.query("select * from orders where amount > ?", [100])
db.one("select count(*) as n from orders")
db.exec("update orders set status = ? where id = ?", ["paid", id])
db.tx(|t| { t.insert(...); t.update(...); })   // one connection; any error rolls back

// No query per row! One query for the related rows / counts:
deals = db.attach(deals, "companies", "company_id", "company");       // d.company: row or ()
companies = db.attach_count(companies, "deals", "company_id", "deals"); // c.deals: int, 0 if none
```

Filter operators: `eq ne gt gte lt lte in nin contains starts ends between
is_null`. `contains/starts/ends` ignore case, Cyrillic included, identically on
SQLite and Postgres (`lower()` in SQLite is replaced by a Unicode one, so your own
`lower(...)` in raw SQL works for Cyrillic too).

Rhai trap: `for r in rows { r.x = 1 }` changes a COPY — the array is untouched.
Use `for i in 0..rows.len() { rows[i].x = 1; }` (`rhaix check` warns).

```rhai
db.find("orders", #{ amount: #{ gte: 100, lt: 1000 }, status: #{ in: ["new", "paid"] } })
db.find("orders", #{ customer: #{ contains: q } })
```

`options` accepts only `sort`, `limit`, `skip`, `fields`. An unknown key is an
error, not silence.

**SQLite has no boolean type.** `done` comes back as `0`/`1`. In markup that is
fine (`@if={t.done}`, `!t.done` both work), but plain Rhai `if t.done` needs
`if bool(t.done)`.

Config, `rhaix.toml`:

```toml
[server]
port = 3000
# trust_proxy = true      # only behind your own proxy: req.ip from X-Forwarded-For

[db]
driver = "sqlite"                 # sqlite | postgres
url = "data/app.db"               # relative to the project root, not the working dir
# driver = "postgres"
# url = "postgres://user:pass@host:5432/dbname"

[app]
csrf = true               # default
session_days = 30
tz_offset = "+03:00"
http_timeout = 10
locale = "uk"             # default locale for t(); files in locales/*.toml

# [mail] enables real SMTP (build with the `mail` feature); without it mail.send logs
# [mail]
# from = "App <noreply@example.com>"
# smtp_host = "smtp.example.com"
# smtp_port = 587
# smtp_user = "..."
# smtp_pass = "..."
```

The session signing key comes from `RHAIX_SECRET`, then `[app] secret`, then a
`.rhaix-secret` file created by `rhaix dev`. In production, set `RHAIX_SECRET`.

Drivers: `sqlite` (default) and `postgres`. The portable layer (`db.find/get/…`)
and `?` placeholders are identical on both — switching driver is a config change,
not a code change. `rhaix build` reads `[db] driver` and compiles only that
driver into the binary, so a SQLite app carries none of the Postgres
dependencies. Two Postgres specifics to know: the portable layer assumes a
primary key column named `id` (a `serial`/`bigserial`); and in **native** queries
you still write `?` placeholders (the driver rewrites them to `$1, $2, …`), so
do not mix in `$1` yourself.

## Sessions and CSRF

```rhai
session.set("user", name);
session.user                      // shorthand for session.get("user")
session.clear();                  // logout
```

A session is a **signed cookie**, not server state: the app stays one binary you
can run twice behind a load balancer. The client can read the contents (base64,
not encryption) but cannot change them. Keep it under ~4 KB; put ids in the
session and data in the database. A session cannot be revoked server-side.
It slides: once half of `session_days` has passed, any request reissues the
cookie for the full lifetime. Responses with `Set-Cookie` get
`Cache-Control: private, no-store` unless the script set caching.

Rate limiting (password guessing, form spam, API clients):

```rhai
let attempts = `login:${req.ip}:${username.to_lower()}`;   // include the user name
if !state.allow(attempts, 5, 300) {                      // 5 per 5 minutes
    res.status(429);
    error = `Try again in ${state.retry_after(attempts)} s`;
} else if verify_password(password, user.password) {
    state.reset(attempts);
}
```

Counters are per process (not shared between copies, cleared on restart).

Roles and permissions (full recipe: examples/cookbook middleware.rhx +
scripts/access.rhai): keep only the user id in the session; in middleware.rhx
load the user once into `page.user` (the page sees the same `page`); map path
prefixes to permissions (`req.path == p || req.path.starts_with(p + "/")`);
pages test `can(page.user, "perm")`, never the role name; the action handler
re-checks `can(...)` — hiding a button is not authorization. Deny an htmx
button with `res.status(403); hx.toast(...); hx.reswap("none"); return "";`.
Redirect back via `url("/login", #{ next: req.url })`, and only follow `next`
if it starts with "/" and not "//".
`req.ip` is the TCP peer; behind your own proxy set `[server] trust_proxy = true`
to read the last `X-Forwarded-For` entry — never otherwise, it is forgeable.

**CSRF needs nothing from you.** A form that changes data gets a hidden field; a
non-form element with `hx-post`/`hx-put`/`hx-patch`/`hx-delete` gets an
`hx-headers` attribute. Requests with a method other than GET/HEAD/OPTIONS and
no valid token are refused with 403 before `middleware.rhx` runs.

Edge cases: dynamic `method={m}` → put `<rhaix:csrf />` inside the form by hand;
your own `hx-headers` → add `#{"x-csrf-token": csrf.token}` yourself;
`data-no-csrf` opts one element out.

## Calling other services

```rhai
let r = http.get("https://api.example.com/rates");
let rate = if r.ok { r.json.usd } else { () };

http.post(url, #{ title: title })                       // map/array → JSON body
http.get(url, #{ Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` })
```

Synchronous — no `await`. Response map: `status`, `ok`, `body`, `json`,
`headers`, `error`. A network failure gives `ok: false`, never an exception, so
no `try` is needed. Only `http://` and `https://` are accepted.

## Helpers

```rhai
url("/orders", #{ q: q, page: n })   // the only correct way to build a link
now() today() date(v) date(v, "DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm") datetime(v) timestamp(s)
days(n) hours(n) minutes(n)
slug(s) cut(s, n) strip_tags(s) capitalize(s) is_blank(v)
money(v) money(v, 0) percent(a, b)
uuid() random_id() sha256(s)
hash_password(pw) verify_password(pw, hash)   // Argon2id — for passwords, not sha256()
validate(values, rules) paginate(total, per, page)   // see the batteries section
csv(rows, #{ columns: [...], titles: [...], sep: ";", decimal: "," })
json(v)              // for <script> only — escapes tag-closing sequences
json_encode(v) json_decode(s)
raw(v) bool(v)
```

Date pattern tokens: `YYYY YY MM M DD D HH H mm m ss s`; text in double quotes
is kept verbatim. `date()` accepts both a timestamp and a database string.
Parsing is strict: `2026-02-31`, `2026-02-29` (non-leap), `25:00`, `12:60` are
not dates — `timestamp()` gives `()`, `date()` "", `validate` rule `date` fails.

## Form validation, pagination, uploads, mail

```rhai
// validate(values, rules) -> map of field -> message (empty if valid)
let errors = validate(req.all_form(), #{
    name:  "required|min:2",
    email: "required|email",
    age:   "int|between:18,120",
    site:  "url",
    pass:  "required|min:8",
    again: "same:pass",
    role:  "in:user,admin",
});
if !errors.is_empty() { res.status(422); }
// rules: required email url int number min:N max:N between:a,b same:field in:a,b,c
// min/max compare by value on int/number fields, by length otherwise

// paginate(total, per_page, page) -> map; page is clamped to 1..=pages
let p = paginate(db.count("orders"), 20, req.query_int("page") ?? 1);
db.find("orders", #{}, #{ sort: "id desc", limit: 20, skip: p.skip });
// p: page pages per_page total skip from to has_prev has_next prev next first last window

// admin table in one call: sort + filters + pages, all in the URL
let g = db.grid("orders", req, #{
    sort: ["id", "customer", "amount"],        // whitelist: ?sort= outside it is ignored
    order: "id desc",                          // NOT `default` — reserved word in Rhai
    filters: #{ status: "eq", customer: "contains", amount: "between" },  // between: amount_from/amount_to
    per_page: 20,
    where: #{ owner_id: page.user.id },        // applied last, the URL cannot override it
});
// g: rows page total sort dir values sort_url arrow page_url prev_url next_url reset_url filtered
// markup: href={g.sort_url.amount}  {{ g.arrow.amount }}  href={g.page_url[`${n}`]}
// operators: eq ne contains starts ends gt gte lt lte between; unknown option/operator is an error

// file uploads (multipart/form-data forms only)
let f = req.file("doc");          // first upload or (); also req.files(name), req.has_file(name)
if f != () {
    // f.filename f.content_type f.size f.is_image f.extension f.text()
    f.save("public/uploads/" + random_id() + "." + f.extension);   // path checked: no absolute, no ..
}

// CSV export: escapes per RFC 4180, defuses formula cells (=, +, -, @ get a leading ')
// rows of maps need `columns` (maps have no field order); arrays of arrays go as is
res.download("orders.csv", csv(orders, #{
    columns: ["id", "customer", "amount"], titles: ["No", "Customer", "Amount"],
    sep: ";", decimal: ",",     // Excel in comma-decimal locales
}));
// res.download: string or blob; type from extension; UTF-8 filename encoded;
// BOM added to CSV; stops rendering. Behind hx-boost a GET download becomes
// HX-Redirect to the same URL (the script runs twice — keep exports on GET).

// mail (dev: logs the message; real SMTP behind the `mail` build feature + [mail] config)
mail.send(#{ to: "x@y.co", subject: "Hi", text: "...", html: "<p>...</p>" });

// i18n: locales/<lang>.toml, read through the same Files trait
t("greeting")                 // current locale -> default locale -> the key itself
t("items", #{ count: 3 })     // "{count}" placeholders
set_locale("en"); locale()    // usually in middleware.rhx; unknown locale is ignored

// markdown (behind the `markdown` build feature): raw HTML is escaped, not
// passed through, and link/image URLs are scheme-checked — safe by construction
{{ markdown(post.body) }}
```

Validation rules in full: `required email url int number bool date min:N max:N
between:a,b len:N same:field different:field in:a,b not_in:a,b starts:x ends:x
alpha alnum`.

## Client: errors swap, toasts and modals are yours

Two layers: the **core** `/_rhaix/rhaix.js` (asset registry, non-2xx swapping,
style dedup — never replace it) and the **interface** `/_rhaix/ui.js` (toasts,
modal `<dialog>` — yours to replace).

htmx only swaps `2xx` responses by default and silently drops the rest. In
rhaix `res.status(...)` is an ordinary response (422 with errors, 403 with an
explanation, 404/500 with diagnostics), so the core overrides
`htmx.config.responseHandling` to swap them (204 excepted) — nothing to do in
the project.

Validation-under-fields is a component, not a built-in tag:

```rhai
components/Field.rhx
---
let name = props.name; let label = props.label;
let value = props.value ?? ""; let error = props.error;
---
<p class="field">
  <label>{{ label }}<br><input name={name} value={value} @class={#{"invalid": error != ()}}></label>
  <span class="error" @if={error}>{{ error }}</span>
</p>
```
```
<Field name="email" label="Email" value={form.email} error={errors.email} />
```

Toasts: `hx.toast(message, type)` → event `showToast` → `ui.js` draws into
`#toasts` (created if missing). Types: info, success, error, warning. Several
toasts per request arrive as one detail with an `items` array. Override just
the drawing in `public/*.js` — `window.__rhaix.toast = (message, type) => …`,
`window.__rhaix.toastTimeout = 8000` — read at event time. Default styles use
`:where()`, so any project CSS wins.

Flash: toasts on a response that redirects (`res.redirect`, `hx.redirect`,
`hx.refresh`) are kept in the session and delivered once with the next
non-redirect response — as `showToast` to htmx, as
`<script type="application/json" data-rhx-toasts>` in a full page (which is
also how toasts of a plain non-htmx page load arrive). So
`hx.toast("Welcome"); res.redirect("/admin")` just works.

`<dialog>` opens itself as a real modal (native backdrop, Esc, focus trap) —
`ui.js` calls `showModal()` for every `<dialog>`, wherever it appears
(first load, fragment, `@oob`). Add `data-plain` to opt a specific dialog out.

Replace the whole interface: `rhaix eject ui` copies it to
`public/rhaix-ui.js`, which is then loaded instead of `/_rhaix/ui.js`. An empty
file disables toasts and auto-modals.

## Shared functions

```rhai
// scripts/orders.rhai — no import anywhere
fn status_label(status) {
    switch status { "new" => "New", "paid" => "Paid", _ => status }
}
```

Visible from every `.rhx`, in frontmatter and in `{{ }}`. Loaded once at
startup, so editing them needs a `rhaix dev` restart (it says so in the console).

## Component assets

```html
<div class="card">…</div>
<style>.card { border: 1px solid #ddd }</style>
<script>console.log({{ json(props) }})</script>
```

`<style>` is hoisted into `<rhaix:head/>`, `<script>` into `<rhaix:scripts/>`,
both deduplicated by content hash. `<style scoped>` narrows selectors to the
file's own markup: every element of that file gets `data-rhx-<hash8>` and
`[data-rhx-…]` is appended to the last compound selector. Slot content stays in
the parent's scope; `@keyframes` is left alone; `:root` will not match. A script runs **once per page lifetime**,
even if its component arrives through several HTMX swaps. htmx is already
loaded when it runs; `public/*.js` (deferred) are not yet — use them from
event handlers. `<style>` is global
in v1 — scoping is v1.1. There are no islands and no `<script client>`.

---

## Two Rhai facts that bite

1. `loop` is a keyword — loop counters live in `iter`.
2. Many string methods mutate in place. rhaix overrides `trim()` so it both
   trims and returns the value, but other in-place methods still behave the
   Rhai way.

## Method-specific logic in one file

```rhai
---
if req.method == "POST" {
    let title = req.form("title").trim();
    if is_blank(title) {
        res.status(422);          // same page, with errors
    } else {
        db.insert("todos", #{ title: title });
        hx.toast("Added", "success");
    }
}
if req.method == "DELETE" {
    db.delete("todos", req.query_int("id"));
    return "";                    // empty body — HTMX removes the element
}
let todos = db.find("todos", #{}, #{ sort: "id desc" });
---
```

Returning a value from frontmatter makes it the response body, skipping markup.

## JSON API

`api/**/*.rhx` serves `/api/<path>` and differs from a page in six ways:
`application/json`, never wrapped in a layout, a returned map or array is
serialised to JSON automatically, errors and 404 come back as `{"error": "..."}`,
**no session**, and CSRF is not checked.

```rhai
api/orders.rhx
---
if req.method == "POST" {
    let sent = req.json();                    // () when the body is not JSON
    let errors = validate(sent, #{ customer: "required|min:2" });
    if !errors.is_empty() { res.status(422); return #{ errors: errors }; }
    res.status(201);
    return db.get("orders", db.insert("orders", sent));
}
return #{ data: db.find("orders") };
---
```

The missing session is deliberate: a route that skips CSRF must not read
cookies, or another site could act as the logged-in user. Authenticate with a
header token in `middleware.rhx`. For JSON *with* a session, use a normal page
with `page.layout = false` and `res.header("content-type", ...)`.

CORS for `api/` only (pages never get it — they carry the cookie session):

```toml
[api]
cors = ["https://app.example.com"]   # or "*" (safe: api/ has no cookies)
openapi = true                       # serve /api/openapi.json (off by default)
title = "Orders API"                 # info.title; defaults to the project dir name
version = "1.0.0"
```

Preflight is answered before any script; errors and 404 under /api also get
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

OpenAPI 3.1 is derived from the files, no annotations: `rhaix openapi [-o file]`.
Paths/params from file names; methods from `if req.method == "X" { … }` blocks
(the rest of the file is GET; `req.method != "X"` guard → X only); query params
and types from `req.query_int("page")` etc.; JSON body schema from
`validate(sent, #{ … })` rules; response codes from `res.status(N)` in that
branch; summary from the leading comment; bearer + 401/429 from the `/api`
block of middleware.rhx.

## Live updates

```rhai
db.insert("orders", o);
live.send("orders");                       // or live.send("orders", #{ id: id })
```

```html
<div id="orders" hx-get="/orders" hx-trigger="live:orders from:body"
     hx-select="#orders" hx-target="this" hx-swap="outerHTML">…</div>
```

The server sends only "topic changed"; each page re-fetches with its own
session, so nothing leaks. The core opens one SSE to `/_rhaix/live` for all
topics on the page (`hx-trigger="live:…"` or `data-live="a b"`), fires
`live:<topic>` on <body>, and after a reconnect fires every topic with
`{ reconnected: true }`. Topic: `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}`. Per process (not shared
between copies behind a balancer).

## Native Rust functions

```rust
// native/lib.rs
use rhaix_server::rhai::Engine;           // use this re-export, not your own `rhai`
pub fn register(engine: &mut Engine) {
    engine.register_fn("fib", |n: i64| -> i64 { /* … */ n });
}
```

`rhaix build` compiles it into the binary; `rhaix dev` / `rhaix serve` see
`native/` and build a server with it via cargo (target/rhaix-native), templates
still reload live. Extra crates: `native/dependencies.toml` (`regex = "1"`).
Embedding: `Config::load(".", None)?.with_native(register)`. A function of the
same name in scripts/*.rhai overrides the Rust one.

## Commands

```bash
rhaix dev <dir>      # live reload, diagnostics in the browser
rhaix serve <dir>    # production from disk: frozen cache, compression
rhaix build <dir>    # one binary with every file embedded
rhaix new <dir>      # project skeleton
rhaix check <dir>    # compile everything without starting; --json for CI; warns
                     # (exit 0) on: layout without <rhaix:head/>, `{x}` in text
                     # (literal — use {{ x }}), @class with selected/checked/…
                     # (use @attr), unknown rhaix.toml keys, `for r in rows
                     # { r.x = … }` (assigns a copy)
rhaix openapi <dir>  # OpenAPI 3.1 of api/ derived from the files; -o file
rhaix eject ui       # copy the built-in toasts/modals into public/rhaix-ui.js to own them
```

## Not in v1, on purpose

- **Islands, client components, partial hydration.** Interactivity is HTMX
  attributes, `public/*.js` and hoisted component `<script>`. This is a design
  decision, not a gap.
- **Scoped slots, `@key` morph swaps, `@transition`** — v1.1.
- **MongoDB and SurrealDB drivers** — the `DbDriver` trait is ready for them,
  the drivers are not written. `sqlite` and `postgres` ship.
- **Rename and find-references** in the editor. Diagnostics, go-to-component
  and completion do exist — `editors/vscode` plus the `rhaix-lsp` server.

Behind build features (enabled automatically by `rhaix build` when the project
uses them): `postgres`, `mail` (real SMTP), `markdown`.
